correctness.rationale: Intersection theory for a plane blowup at five points in general position gives precisely the listed 40 intersections. All positive multiplicities for distinct curves are one, so these pairwise intersections are transverse. The graph is triangle-free, so distinct branches cannot form triple points. The 16 rational components and the connected graph give Picard torus rank 25, with character lattice the signed integral cycle kernel by normalization. I used a different spanning tree: all five Q–E_i edges together with the ten edges from each L_ij to its smaller indexed E_i. The reduced incidence minor is unimodular, with complement coordinates giving an integral cycle basis. Independent exact operations on uI−G give the stated seven diagonals. In particular, after constant unit elimination the (3,2) coupled block is [[−u(u+1),−(u²+u+1)],[u+1,u²+u+1]], which admits a unit by subtracting u times its first column from the second; it leaves (u+1)(u³−1) up to sign. For (4,1) the coupled entries −u and u+1 in one column produce a unit by row addition and leave (u+1)(u²+1) together with the other claimed factors. All transformations specialize integrally at every q. Frobenius fixed points are the prime-to-characteristic dual of the specialized cokernel: det(qI−G) is a unit modulo the characteristic since G is invertible over Z. This proves the abstract point-group table, not only orders. At odd q the two mixed rows have five and seven even factors respectively, versus six and eight for their rationally suggested split products. The conclusion is conditional on a permutation-model blowup, with no small-field realizability assumption or general signed-Weyl classification.

value.rationale: The ordinary permutation forms are a natural full family of five-point blowups. The calculation determines their exact integral point-group invariants in every realization, and two mixed types supply concrete instances where rational Frobenius data fail to recover odd-field 2-primary structure. Those invariant factors are more informative than orders, a single table row, or an arbitrary field sample.
